note: Real-ELF ProgramTest for the CHECKPOINTED aggregate-retirement chain -- the terminal lifecycle of a market, in BOTH the shapes a market can have. THE CATEGORICAL WALK is the four-instruction chain that shipped: prepare hands the Claims aggregate to Core, close-vault closes HoardPrincipal, close-replay closes the Custody replay, finish closes the checkpoint, the Market and the RentCredit and pays every classified rent lamport to the immutable refund wallet. THE REFUNDING WALK is the same four packets three accounts wider -- the escrow Position decision 0025 seats the failure coordinate in, its protocol-Position admission, and the Market's linked ProductBasisV3 record -- whose prepare BURNS a column no certificate pays, and whose four hostiles refuse that burn by discriminant. Until 2026-09-06 only the categorical walk ran here, so the entire terminal lifecycle of the market shape the burn exists for was invisible to the census while its own suite was green: the same instrument gap this tier was built to close, one market shape over. Campaign: crates/dclutch-svm-harness/tests/market_retirement_v1_lifecycle.rs, tests `checkpointed_retirement_is_packet_bounded_resumable_and_conserving`, `a_refunding_market_retires_once_the_closure_burns_its_failure_column` and `the_closure_burn_refuses_its_four_hostiles_by_discriminant`. EVERY BINDING BELOW WAS AUTHORED FROM FOLDED EVIDENCE, NEVER FROM WHAT THE CAMPAIGN OUGHT TO TOUCH: the outcomes, the invoked programs and the refusal codes are the ones the runtime reported in a 21-transaction fold, and each label was checked to carry exactly one outcome AND one refusal code before it was written down. THE COMPUTE FIGURES IN EVERY NOTE ARE FROM ONE FOLD, re-taken 2026-09-06 at `42c3bb931` on Linux under platform-tools v1.53; the twelve categorical rows carried figures from an earlier fold on different artifacts and most of them moved, so they are restated here rather than left to disagree with the document they are supposed to describe. Two conservatisms are deliberate. (1) `core/commit_checkpoint#<magic>` and `core/finish_checkpoint_retirement#...` are bound ONLY to the transactions that COMMITTED. A suffix that refuses inside execute_direct_custody_suffix entered the arm but never reached the commit those route ids name, and binding it there would credit a commit that did not happen. (2) `program` is `core` on every row, because every transaction here is a top-level Core instruction; the Claims, Custody, Rent and SPL Token frames the chain drives by CPI are named in each row's note and, where a Claims refusal is the last word, in the refusal id itself.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: prepare against a Claims aggregate reassigned to the System program
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the first census evidence of the Claims handoff route of any kind. Core dispatches the DCLTCRQ1 prepare, authenticates the market and the four roles, and CPIs into Claims, which refuses the reassigned aggregate as Custom(0x5502) after 117,154 CU. Claims AND Core appear in the finalized logs, which is what makes the handoff a corroborated route rather than an inference from the instruction data.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-vault suffix before the Claims handoff
bindings.note: HOSTILE. A suffix cannot mint authority before the prepare: the checkpoint account is still the live Claims aggregate, and Core refuses as Custom(0x3005) at 26,989 CU with no other program in the frame. This is the phase ordering of the chain stated as a refusal.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: prepare hands the Claims aggregate to Core
bindings.note: The chain's first act, accepted: 139,884 CU, Claims and Core in the frame. Afterwards the aggregate is Core-owned, 256 bytes, and holds the SAME lamports it held as a Claims account -- the campaign asserts that equality and that the RentCredit did not move, so the refund is retained in the handed-off account rather than relabelled.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: prepare replayed against a ClaimsClosed checkpoint
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and an observation worth the row on its own: the replayed prepare refuses as Custom(0x300b) at 63,851 CU with CLAIMS NEVER INVOKED. The guard fires inside Core, before the handoff CPI -- so the Claims route is deliberately NOT bound here, and the replay costs a third of the accepted prepare rather than the whole of it.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-vault against a checkpoint reassigned away from Core
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The ClaimsClosed checkpoint reassigned to the Claims program: Custom(0x3005), 36,409 CU, Core alone. The campaign asserts the refusal closes and refunds nothing across Core, Claims, Custody and Rent state.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-replay before the HoardPrincipal vault closes
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The two suffixes are ORDERED: the Custody replay cannot close while the HoardPrincipal vault is live. Custom(0x3005), 36,757 CU, Core alone.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-vault closes the HoardPrincipal vault
bindings.note: 126,725 CU across Core, Custody and the runtime's SPL Token program (TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA). The HoardPrincipal vault is gone afterwards while the Market and the RentCredit are still there -- the chain closes one compartment per transaction and is resumable between them, which is the whole point of checkpointing it.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-vault replayed against a HoardVaultClosed checkpoint
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The checkpoint has advanced, so the same instruction is now out of phase: Custom(0x3005), 36,750 CU. The campaign asserts the refusal is byte- and lamport-atomic across the whole joined snapshot.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-replay closes the Custody replay
bindings.note: 117,503 CU, Core and Custody. No SPL Token frame this time: the replay is a state account, not a token vault, which is visible in the logs and is the difference between the two suffixes the shared CHECKPOINT_RETIREMENT_CUSTODY_SUFFIX_BYTES_V1 length hides.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: close-replay replayed against a CustodyReplayClosed checkpoint
bindings.note: HOSTILE. Custom(0x3005), 36,746 CU. Four distinct hostiles in this campaign share this code and each carries its own label, because the code alone cannot tell them apart and a shared label would let the census read all four off whichever ran first.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: finish with the immutable refund wallet substituted
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the cheapest refusal in the chain: Custom(0x3001) at 7,850 CU. The refund wallet is pinned by the frame itself, so substituting it dies in account-frame validation before any magic arm runs -- which is why `core/finish_checkpoint_retirement#...` is NOT bound to this row.

bindings.label: retirement checkpoint: finish closes checkpoint, Market and RentCredit
bindings.note: The terminal act: 102,967 CU across Core and Rent. Afterwards the checkpoint, the Market, the RentCredit, the Custody replay and the Hoard vault are all gone, the Source receipt is byte-identical to its prestate, and the immutable refund wallet has gained exactly the plan's expected_refund_delta -- every classified rent lamport arriving exactly once.

bindings.label: refunding retirement: prepare burns the failure column
bindings.note: THE FIRST COMPLETE RETIREMENT OF A REFUNDING MARKET the census has ever seen. 148,544 CU across Core and Claims on a THIRTY-EIGHT-account frame -- the categorical prepare's thirty-five plus the escrow Position, its admission and the linked ProductBasisV3 record, at metas 35, 36 and 37 -- and 1,089 wire bytes against the categorical 1,083, which is six: three more table-resolved account indexes in the instruction's list and three more in the lookup's index arrays, with no static key and no request byte moving. Against the identical prestate WITHOUT those three accounts the same act refuses 0x5503; that negative control is a_seated_failure_column_refuses_the_claims_handoff_by_name, which submits nothing and so is not in this fold. The burn costs 8,660 CU here (139,884 categorical, 148,544 refunding) and the poststate is what makes it a burn rather than a tolerance: the escrow's Position and admission are CLOSED, not emptied, and their rent is in the checkpoint.

bindings.label: refunding retirement: close vault
bindings.note: 124,440 CU across Core, Custody and the runtime's SPL Token program, on the same thirty-eight-account frame at 1,145 wire bytes. The three trailing accounts are carried and never read: aggregate_retirement_journal requires ONE frame per retirement, so a suffix packet presents what the prepare presented. That is the whole cost of the choice -- about 715 CU per unread account against the categorical 126,725 -- and it buys a journal whose four operations are one shape.

bindings.label: refunding retirement: close replay
bindings.note: 110,718 CU across Core and Custody, no token frame, 1,145 wire bytes. Same shape, same carried tail.

bindings.label: refunding retirement: finish
bindings.note: 96,182 CU across Core and Rent, 1,025 wire bytes, and the Market reaches Retired. The refund wallet's rise carries the escrow pair's rent INSIDE expected_refund_delta rather than beside it: the pair surrendered its lamports to the checkpoint at prepare, the checkpoint surrenders them here, and the campaign asserts the wallet to the lamport.

bindings.label: burn hostile: not the derived escrow
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The frame's trailing Position is a CANONICAL protocol-Position pair at another owner, planted holding exactly the residue at exactly the failure coordinate -- so every rule stated against the Position's own bytes admits it, and what refuses it is re-deriving the owner off the aggregate. Custom(0x5010) at 123,372 CU, Claims in the frame. It is the same accusation the complete-set gate, the signed-delta waist and the founding already raise for 'the named Position is not this Market's escrow', so the burn is the fourth route to one page.

bindings.label: burn hostile: substituted basis record
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the first census evidence of this discriminant. A VALID categorical ProductBasisV3 this Market was not founded on: the join is content-addressed -- the aggregate's basis_id IS the record's semantic identity under semantic_basis_id_v3 -- so a substitution cannot be made to agree. Custom(0x5506) at 119,415 CU. It is split from Identity because it sends its reader to another program's record entirely, and it is also the categorical case: a record that does not refund on failure licenses no burn.

bindings.label: burn hostile: a stranger holds part of the column
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The aggregate carries one unit MORE at the failure coordinate than the escrow holds. That unit is in hands that can be paid, so it is an outstanding liability rather than a residue, and the closure refuses the conjunct it always refused: Custom(0x5503) at 127,519 CU. The residue rule is an EQUALITY against the escrow's own balance and nothing weaker.

bindings.label: burn hostile: the escrow holds a tradeable claim
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The escrow holds the residue AND an ordinary claim: its holder is keyless but that second claim is not worthless, and burning the whole Position would destroy a payable one. Custom(0x5503) at 127,065 CU -- the same discriminant as the stranger above, because it is the same accusation from the other side of the equality.

bindings.label: burn hostiles: the honest packet still burns
bindings.note: THE POSITIVE CONTROL, submitted LAST from the same fixture the four hostiles ran against, so a hostile that refused because the setup was broken takes this row down with it. 141,044 CU, Claims in the frame, and the escrow Position is gone afterwards. Its CU differs from the honest walk's 148,544 because the hostiles warp the fixture's slot between submissions to get fresh blockhashes; the difference is the fixture's, not the route's.
